summary: Customer reports unexpected auto-rollbacks during low traffic; suspected false positives due to stale SLO monitors
description:
Issue summary
- Lakeview Analytics reports their model rollouts are being rolled back automatically even when application traffic is minimal. They suspect false-positive SLO breaches.

Customer impact
- 3 rollbacks in ~24 hours (all during off-peak / low QPS), causing confusion and delayed rollout of a planned model version.
- Customer concern: “automation is unstable / flapping,” and they want confirmation the system won’t rollback on bad signal.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: lakeview-dedicated-us-east
- Region: us-east
- Rollout type: canary (5% -> 25% planned)
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/completions (primary), /v1/embeddings (secondary)

What customer observed
- Console showed "Latency SLO breached" verdict followed immediately by auto-rollback.
- When they checked their own logs, they saw only a handful of requests during the window, and some requests were retries.
- They also noted the SLO dashboard was briefly missing data (“No data” gaps).

Steps to reproduce (as reported)
1) Start rollout for model version v2025.02.17-rc1 at 5% canary.
2) Leave rollout running overnight (low traffic).
3) Receive Slack notification from Redwood Incident Bot: auto-rollback executed.

Notes / early hypotheses
- Low-traffic windows may be triggering noisy percentiles / error-rate calculation artifacts.
- Monitor staleness / gaps: controller may be treating missing monitor data as breach (fail-closed behavior) or using a cached stale breach result.
- Potential mismatch between monitor evaluation window and controller polling cadence (leading to repeated triggers on the same old datapoint).

Requested by customer
- Confirm minimum-traffic guardrail exists and is working.
- Clarify behavior under monitor outages (“no data”): do we rollback or pause?
- Provide a mitigation they can apply immediately (policy override, cooldown, or pause automation) while we fix.

Links / references
- Internal: Slack #eng-sre thread (monitor staleness + flapping): 1707248822
- Internal: Slack #architecture discussion (fail-open vs fail-closed): 1707489004
- Dashboard: Rollout SLO - lakeview-dedicated-us-east (internal link)
- Runbook: Auto-rollback on SLO breach (Confluence)
comments: 2025-02-18 09:12 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — First response to customer via support channel. Asked for rollout ID(s), timestamps, and whether they saw gaps in their telemetry. Suggested immediate mitigation: pause auto-rollback policy on the affected route until we validate monitors (per runbook).

2025-02-18 10:03 PT — Customer (Lakeview Analytics) — Provided timestamps for 3 rollbacks: 02/17 23:41 PT, 02/18 02:09 PT, 02/18 04:22 PT. Noted traffic was <1 rps during these windows. Also attached screenshot showing “Latency P95 breach” with only ~20 requests in the chart tooltip.

2025-02-18 10:40 PT — Aisha Bello (SRE) — Checked SLO dashboard panels: multiple “No data” gaps on latency histogram for the canary route label during the breach windows. Error-rate panel showed 1–2 5xx, but denominator extremely low. Hypothesis: low denominator + partial ingestion delay causing spiky burn-rate/threshold evaluation.

2025-02-18 11:25 PT — Nadia Rahman (Telemetry) — Confirmed ingestion delay spikes in us-east around 02:00–05:00 PT due to a backpressure event on one of the metric relays. Some time series were late by 6–10 minutes. Not all labels were consistently present (route tag occasionally missing on canary traffic due to sampling bug). Referenced dependency INT-3310 (missing labels).

2025-02-18 12:10 PT — Benji Okafor (Platform Control Plane) — Looked at rollout-controller decision traces. Found repeated evaluations using the last non-empty monitor response for up to ~15 minutes when monitor query returned empty (cached). That stale value was a breach, so controller re-triggered rollback even after traffic stopped. This indicates a staleness handling gap in monitor client / evaluator pipeline.

2025-02-18 13:02 PT — Miles Thornton (Staff SRE) — Proposed change: introduce explicit verdict=UNKNOWN when monitor is stale/unavailable or returns empty for required series; do not rollback on UNKNOWN (default fail-open), but emit event + page/ticket depending on tier. Also require min_requests/min_tokens in window before evaluating latency percentiles. Coordinating with control plane team on hotfix.

2025-02-19 09:18 PT — Jordan Lee (Policy Engine) — Confirmed current policy defaults for min traffic were configured at the route level, but the Lakeview policy was created before min-traffic fields were rolled out and is missing them (falls back to permissive defaults). We can apply a policy patch immediately for this tenant while code fix is in progress.

2025-02-19 10:05 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Updated customer: we’ve identified two contributing factors (monitor data gaps + stale cached breach result). Applied a temporary mitigation: increased cooldown to 60m and set min_requests=200 for /v1/chat/completions canary policy; also recommended keeping auto-rollback paused overnight until patch is deployed. Customer acknowledged.

2025-02-20 16:44 PT — Benji Okafor (Platform Control Plane) — Opened/linked PR for guardrail: github/redwood/pr-18546 (treat stale/unavailable monitor as UNKNOWN; prevent rollback; log decision trace). Added evaluator metric: monitor_stale_count and unknown_verdict_count.

2025-02-21 11:30 PT — Sergio Costa (Observability) — Updated dashboard panel to surface “Monitor freshness / last datapoint age” and to show UNKNOWN verdict rate. Coordinated alert routing: UNKNOWN should ticket (not page) for dedicated unless prolonged (>30m).

2025-02-24 09:55 PT — Leila Farouk (QA) — Ran synthetic low-traffic test in staging: 10–30 requests/window with forced metric gaps. Expected behavior after patch: controller emits UNKNOWN + no rollback; logs include reason=MONITOR_STALE and reason=INSUFFICIENT_TRAFFIC. Test passed.

2025-02-25 14:20 PT — Miles Thornton (Staff SRE) — Patch deployed to prod us-east rollout-controller. Verified on Lakeview route with policy unpaused: no further rollbacks overnight; UNKNOWN events observed during a brief telemetry delay without action. Closing as resolved; follow-ups tracked on linked engineering work.
resolution: Resolved by (1) policy mitigation for the customer (min_requests + longer cooldown) and (2) rollout-controller guardrail hotfix to prevent auto-rollback when monitors are stale/unavailable (explicit UNKNOWN verdict handling) plus improved freshness visibility in dashboards. Customer confirmed stability (no unexpected rollbacks) after deployment.
next_steps: 1) Complete monitor labeling migration to reduce empty-series cases (track INT-3310 + monitor identity rollout). 2) Backfill/validate min-traffic defaults for policies created pre-schema update. 3) Tune alerting so UNKNOWN verdicts generate tickets (not pages) unless prolonged. 4) Add regression test specifically for stale cached breach reuse across empty monitor responses (CI).
